summary: Source-anchored research for Covered queries on sharded collections. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The SHARDING_FILTER stage reports chunkSkips, the number of orphaned documents on the shard; a value above 0 means the shard holds orphaned documents. Huawei Cloud's FAQ uses this check and warns that its command scans all documents on all shard nodes in a collection. The server test covered_shard_key_indexes.js asserts chunkSkips of 0 in its bad-data cases, including the covered one. Sources: https://support.huaweicloud.com/intl/es-us/drs_faq/drs_09_0101.html ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/libs/query/analyze_plan.js

If a query runs through mongos against a sharded collection, an index can cover it only when the index contains the shard key. The manual lists this under the limitations of covered queries. The rule reads the same in the v4.4 manual source, the v7.0 manual and the current manual. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v4.4/core/query-optimization/

The manual defines a covered query as one where all fields in the query, 'both as specified by the application and as needed internally such as for sharding purposes', are part of an index. On a sharded collection, the shard key fields count as fields the query needs. (high confidence)

The 3.0 manual added one exception: a query on a sharded collection that specifies only _id and returns only _id could be covered by the _id index through mongos, even if _id is not the shard key. The v4.4 manual source, the v7.0 manual and the current manual contain no such exception, so older answers and posts that cite it are outdated. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v3.0/source/includes/extracts-parent-fact-covered-query-sharded-collection.yaml ; https://github.com/mongodb/docs/blob/v4.4/source/includes/extracts-parent-fact-covered-query-sharded-collection.yaml ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v7.0/core/query-optimization.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md

A dotted shard key such as {'a.b':1} is satisfied by an index that contains the same path: index {c:1,'a.b':1} covers find({c:true},{_id:0,'a.b':1,c:1}). An index on a parent field does not satisfy a shard key that is a subfield of it. With shard key {'_id.a':1,'_id.b':1} the _id index holds enough data, but the planner does not use it, and the improvement ticket SERVER-33054 is in Backlog, unresolved. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-33054

If a query on a sharded collection runs through mongos, an index covers it only when the index contains the shard key. The manual states this in Query Optimization and again in Limits and Thresholds. Query Optimization also counts fields 'needed internally such as for sharding purposes' among the fields an index must hold. The query planner enforces the rule. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp

Before the fix, no query on a sharded collection run through mongos could be covered. The shard loaded the full document for every match whenever a chunk manager existed (SERVER-5022, created 2012-02-20). Commit 2f7fce0 'SERVER-5022 allow covered queries with shard filter' fixed it in 2.7.6, a development release. The change covers only indexes that contain the shard key, because the shard still checks chunk ownership. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-5022 ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/commit/2f7fce0 ; https://groups.google.com/g/mongodb-user/c/dBHCu7GbSlU/m/q9sVcaU5UvgJ ; https://mongodb.com/docs/v3.0/core/query-optimization/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v2.6/source/core/query-optimization.txt

When _id is the shard key, a covering index must contain _id. With shard key {_id:1}, index {a:1} does not cover find({a:true}, {_id:1, a:1}) (1 document examined). Index {a:1, _id:1} covers it (0 examined). Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/

Since 4.3.1 (SERVER-42390), a document with no value for a shard-key field counts as null there. Before, orphan filtering treated such a document as orphaned and always dropped it. A covered query through an index that contains the shard key therefore returns such a document. The master test shows 1 document returned, 0 examined, chunkSkips 0, and calls this 'weird' because indexes have no 'does not exist' value. (medium confidence) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-42390 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js

In 2013 (SERVER-8405) it was reported that a sharded count skipped the chunk-ownership check. That let counts use covered indexes, but the counts could include orphaned or migrating documents. The ticket proposed, among other options, covered-index chunk-membership checking for indexes that include the shard key, falling back to the full document otherwise. SERVER-5022 (the ticket about the full document always being loaded when there is a chunk manager, which made covered indexes ineffective) is closed as Done with fix version 2.7.6. Current count behavior on sharded clusters was not verified. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-8405 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-5022

When a query takes the IDHACK path (an equality on _id), the planner always fetches the full document and adds a ShardFilterStage if the collection is sharded; the code comment says 'we don't support covered projections'. Such queries are not covered on sharded collections. In 2.6.0 to 2.6.2, IDHackRunner allowed covered _id projections on sharded connections, skipped the sharding filter and returned orphan documents. SERVER-14304 fixed this in 2.6.3, and adding hint({_id:1}) avoided it. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/exec/runtime_planners/classic_runtime_planner/idhack_planner.cpp ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-14304

The position of FETCH relative to SHARDING_FILTER shows why the fetch exists. When the plan is not already fetched, the planner adds a FETCH below SHARDING_FILTER if a shard key field is not provided by the index, or if the index provides the hash of a field whose shard key entry is not hashed. A FETCH above SHARDING_FILTER is added later, for example when there is no projection and the whole document is needed. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp

Orphan filtering, the reason for the shard-key-in-index rule, also applies to reads from secondaries, because every member of a shard replica set keeps chunk metadata. Earlier versions could return orphaned documents from secondaries whatever the read concern. Read concern 'available' skips the check that the correct shard received the query, and it can return orphaned documents during chunk migration. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/distributed-queries.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md

In sharded explain output, the SHARDING_FILTER stage reports chunkSkips, the number of orphaned documents it filtered out. If chunkSkips is not 0 for a shard, orphaned documents exist on that shard. Sources: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/dts/support/how-do-you-clean-up-orphaned-documents-in-a-mongodb-sharded-cluster

The server decides per operation, on each shard, whether to add the shard filter. getExecutorFind and the count path set INCLUDE_SHARD_FILTER when the collection acquisition's sharding description reports the collection as sharded. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

Indexing only the filter and projection fields, without the shard key, leaves a FETCH on every shard. With shard key {_id:'hashed'} and index {a:1}, find({a:true},{_id:0,a:1}) still examines one document. The planner's own comment says the full documents must be fetched prior to shard filtering when the index does not provide a shard-key field. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp

The shard filter reads the shard-key value of each document it checks. If the index scan does not supply every shard-key field, the planner puts a FETCH stage below SHARDING_FILTER, and the query is no longer covered. The planner also adds the FETCH when the index supplies only the hash of a shard-key field that is not itself hashed. SERVER-8405 (2013) had proposed checking chunk membership from the index when the index includes the shard key, and fetching the document otherwise. (high confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-8405

A nested shard key such as {'a.b': 1} can be covered on current master. Index {c:1, 'a.b':1} with projection {_id:0, 'a.b':1, c:1} examines 0 documents. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js

Before 8.2, DISTINCT_SCAN plans for $group on sharded collections had no SHARDING_FILTER, so orphaned documents could supply stale values (SERVER-42160, fixed in 8.2.0-rc0). A feature flag, created in 8.1.0-rc0, covers generating shard-filtered DISTINCT_SCAN plans. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-42160 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-92458

If a covered query on a sharded collection still shows FETCH, check in order: (1) the index lacks a shard-key field; (2) the projection returns a field the index lacks, including _id unless the index holds it or the projection sets _id:0; (3) the query matches null, since {field: null} and {field: {$eq: null}} never cover; (4) the index is hashed, or is multikey on an array field. Causes 2 to 4 also apply to unsharded collections. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed/

Run explain from mongos to check coverage on a sharded collection. A covered plan has an IXSCAN stage that is not a descendant of a FETCH stage. MongoDB's sharding test covered_shard_key_indexes.js checks that executionStats.totalDocsExamined is 0 for covered queries. Through mongos the root execution stage is SINGLE_SHARD or SHARD_MERGE, with each shard's plan under shards. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/libs/query/analyze_plan.js

To cover a query on a sharded collection, add every shard key field to the covering index after the query fields. MongoDB's tests use {c:1,b:1,a:1} for shard key {a:1,b:1}, and {c:1,d:1,a:1,b:1,_id:1} for a filter on c and d. The manual says the ESR rule orders the fields of a covered-query index. (medium confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/

To decide whether a query on a sharded collection can be covered, check: (1) when run on mongos, the index contains the shard key; (2) the same index supplies every field the filter and projection use; (3) for a hashed shard key, the query and projection do not include the hashed fields (the server otherwise fetches documents to rule out orphans; with a compound hashed shard key that has a range prefix, a query on the prefix with a projection that omits hashed fields can be covered); (4) the usual limits hold: no equality-to-null predicate, no array fields from a multikey index, and _id excluded from the projection unless it is indexed. Then confirm with explain from mongos. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-44773

Check coverage by running explain('executionStats') through mongos. A covered plan shows an IXSCAN that is not a descendant of a FETCH, and totalDocsExamined is 0. The server tests assert totalDocsExamined of 0 for covered cases and 1 for uncovered ones. Per-shard plans sit under queryPlanner.winningPlan.shards and executionStats.executionStages.shards. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js

The index must contain every shard key field, including fields that the filter and the projection do not use. In MongoDB's sharding tests, hinting index {a:1,c:1} on shard key {a:1,b:'hashed',c:1} adds a FETCH to find({a:{$gt:25,$lt:29}},{a:1,c:1,_id:0}). On shard key {a:1,b:1}, index {c:1} cannot cover a query that projects a, b and c, while index {c:1,b:1,a:1} can. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/compound_hashed_shard_key_covered_query.js ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js

Hashed indexes can't cover a query. A collection sharded on one hashed field therefore gets no covered query on that field: with shard key {_id:'hashed'}, find({_id:true},{_id:0}) examines one document. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js

Before MongoDB 3.0, an index could not cover a query on a sharded collection through mongos. The 3.0 manual marks the rule with 'versionchanged 3.0: In previous versions, an index cannot cover a query on a sharded collection when run against a mongos.' SERVER-5022 ('full document always loaded for matches if there is a chunk manager') reports that covered indexes were ineffective when shardingState.needShardChunkManager(pq.ns()) is true; the reporter was unsure whether this held in all sharding setups. It is resolved Done with fix version 2.7.6, resolved 2014-09-05. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v3.0/source/includes/extracts-parent-fact-covered-query-sharded-collection.yaml ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-5022

Hashed indexes can't cover a query. The server test for a hashed _id shard key asserts that find({_id:true},{_id:0}) examines 1 document, with the comment "can't be covered since hashed index". A single-field hashed shard-key index therefore cannot be the covering index. A compound hashed shard key such as {a:1, b:'hashed', c:1} can cover queries in current server tests, provided neither the query nor the projection uses the hashed field. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed.md ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/commit/2f7fce0 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/compound_hashed_shard_key_covered_query.js

When the query pins the full shard key by equality, mongos can target one shard. In the r6.0.0 source the planner then omits the shard filter, because shards cannot own orphans for the key ranges they own; the source comment says this may allow a more efficient plan, for example a COUNT_SCAN. When the shard has no routing metadata, the shard filter is also omitted. The predicate still names the shard-key fields, so the index must still contain them to cover the query. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/r6.0.0/src/mongo/db/query/get_executor.cpp ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/

A 3.4-era copy of the manual listed one exception: a query on a sharded collection that filters only on _id and returns only _id could be covered by the _id index through mongos, even if _id is not the shard key. The current manual lists no such exception; its Sharded Collections limit says only that the index must contain the shard key. Do not rely on the _id exception. The release that removed it was not determined. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) Sources: https://mongoing.com/docs/core/query-optimization.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md

The coverage limit applies to queries that arrive through mongos. The planner adds the shard filter only when the command requests it; the source comment reads 'Shard filter was not requested; cmd may not be from a router'. A January 2015 report in the mongodb-user group (about a pre-2.8 server) saw indexOnly true with 0 objects scanned on the shard's mongod, and indexOnly false through mongos. A direct connection does not request the shard filter, so it does not drop orphaned documents. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/query_planner_params.cpp ; https://groups.google.com/g/mongodb-user/c/dBHCu7GbSlU/m/q9sVcaU5UvgJ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v2.6/source/core/query-optimization.txt ; https://mongodb.com/docs/v3.0/core/query-optimization/

Each shard must drop documents it does not own, such as orphaned documents, before it returns results. The SHARDING_FILTER stage does this and needs the shard key value of every candidate document. If the index does not supply every shard key field, the planner adds a FETCH below SHARDING_FILTER so the filter can read the shard key from the document. (high confidence)

The order of the shard key fields inside the index does not matter for covering. Index {a:1,c:1,b:'hashed'} covers queries on shard key {a:1,b:'hashed',c:1}, and index {c:1,b:1,a:1} covers queries on shard key {a:1,b:1}. (high confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/compound_hashed_shard_key_covered_query.js ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md

A hashed shard key field needs only its hash in the index for shard filtering. If the shard key field is hashed and the index holds its hash, the plan needs no FETCH. If the shard key field is ranged and the index holds only a hash of that field, the planner adds a FETCH. If the index holds the raw value of a field whose shard key is hashed, the plan stays covered. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

A find or count that fixes the whole shard key with equality predicates can omit SHARDING_FILTER: {a:true,b:true} on shard key {a:1,b:1}, or {a:true} on shard key {a:'hashed'}. A prefix of a compound shard key, an $in on a shard key field, or a filter on a non-shard-key field keeps the stage. A plan without SHARDING_FILTER can therefore be by design. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

A sharded collection must have an index on the shard key, or a compound index with the shard key as a prefix, and sh.shardCollection() builds the shard key index on an empty collection. That index can itself serve covered queries. In MongoDB's compound-hashed test, the shard key index {a:1,b:'hashed',c:1} covers find({a:0},{a:1,c:1,_id:0}), rejects the orphan documents and uses no FETCH. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-shard-key-indexes/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/compound_hashed_shard_key_covered_query.js

A shard that receives a query uses the most efficient index available, either the shard key index or another eligible index present on the shard. On a sharded collection queried through mongos, an index can only cover a query if it contains the shard key. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/jstests/sharding/covered_shard_key_indexes.js

For distinct and $group on a sharded collection, the hand-built distinct scan chooses an index from the projection alone. With indexes {notShardKey:1} and {notShardKey:1,shardKey:1}, it can pick the first and add a redundant FETCH. SERVER-97235 (Needs Scheduling, opened 2024-11-15) tracks this. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

A document stored on a shard without the shard key field, for example inserted directly on the shard, is returned by both the fetch plan and the covered plan, and chunkSkips stays 0 in both. The test comment calls the covered result 'weird' and attributes it to indexes having no dedicated 'does not exist' value. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

When shard ownership filtering applies, the SHARDING_FILTER stage drops documents that do not belong to the shard, including pending documents from in-progress migrations and orphaned documents from aborted migrations. The explain reference describes SHARDING_FILTER as filtering orphan documents from shards. This is not universal for every read: read concern "available" skips the correct-shard check and can return orphaned documents during migration. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/exec/classic/shard_filter.cpp ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md

A compound shard key needs every one of its fields in the covering index, in any order. With shard key {a:1, b:1}, the server test shows index {c:1, b:1, a:1} covers find({c:true}, {_id:0, a:1, b:1, c:1}) with 0 documents examined. Index {c:1} alone examines 1 document. (high confidence)

Coverage and targeting depend on different things. Coverage needs the shard key inside the index. Targeting needs the shard key, or a prefix of a compound shard key, inside the query predicate; without one, mongos broadcasts to all shards. A covered query with no shard-key predicate is therefore still a scatter-gather query (this follows from the two documented rules). (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md

Adding a shard-key predicate only to steer routing can break a covering index that lacks the shard key. The shard-local query then names a field the index does not hold (SERVER-11991, opened 2013). The reporter asked for a routing-only hint and said putting the shard key in every index 'seems like a hack'. MongoDB closed the ticket as Won't Fix on 2019-11-07. (low confidence)

The _id point-lookup path has returned orphans on sharded collections. In 2.6.0 to 2.6.2 the IDHACK path allowed covered projections on sharded connections, skipped the sharding filter, and returned orphaned documents (SERVER-14304). Release 2.6.3 stopped allowing covered projections there. In current source the express _id lookup is handed the collection's shard filter whenever the filter was requested. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-14304 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/exec/express/plan_executor_express.cpp

Orphan filtering depends on the read concern. Reads with 'available' skip the check that the correct shard received the query and can return orphaned documents. All members of a shard replica set keep chunk metadata, so reads from secondaries do not return orphaned data unless the read concern is 'available'; earlier versions could return orphans from secondaries with any read concern. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/distributed-queries.md
